newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude ends up, rebounding on short covering.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude ends up, rebounding on short covering.

text.p: NYMEX crude ended with slim gains Wednesday, sharply rebounding on short covering after bearish oil inventory data sparked heavy selling that dried up.

"Fundamentally, the APIs were bearish. What happened was there was, after a while, a lack of follow-through to the downside, so shorts started to cover," said John Saucer, analyst with Smith Barney in Houston.
June crude ended two cents up at $21.39 a barrel after falling as low as $20.85.
Chartists noted technical support for spot crude was found near 20.88 area, set by the ACCESS low, the low March 31 and trendline support extending from April 16 on the June chart.
Refined products also retraced steep intraday losses on short covering. June gasoline finished 0.38 cent off at 64.30 cents a gallon after tumbling to as 62.75 cents.
June heating oil settled off 0.06 cent a gallon at 56.42 cents after falling to 55.60 cents.
"The ability for the market to come back says a lot about how resilient the market is," said a New York crude dealer, adding, "but I am not convinced crude is out of the woods yet."
Traders noted it was only two sessions ago that spot crude's upside breakout catapulted it from a $19.50 to $20.50 range in was stuck in for three weeks.
Moreover, traders have said the breakout itself was suspect since it was mostly on short covering rather than on new length which would have signalled longer term confidence in the uptrend.

Still, spot crude stayed clear of its old range even though the American Petroleum Institute (API) said Tuesday evening that for the week ended May 9, crude stocks grew a whopping 6.94 million barrels.
Traders had expected a one million barrel build.
The API also said crude stocks stood 22.9 million barrels above a year ago.

Even more bearish was that gasoline stocks grew a much larger-than-expected 6.51 million barrels when traders had expected a build of only a one million barrels. More builds may be near dealers said noting gasoline production rose to 8.1 million barrels per day (bpd) from 7.8 million bpd.
Gasoline production was spurred on by a sharp rise in refinery run rates that stood at a feverish 96.9 percent versus 94.5 percent last week.

Distillate stocks, comprised of heating oil and diesel, dropped 1.10 million barrels when dealers had expected a build. But, heating oil is out of season, so it did not benefit from the data, dealers said.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
